generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The move of static final versions from `SqlVersion` to a new class `SqlVersions` is a good practice for organization. However, ensure that all references to these constants are updated correctly in the codebase. The introduction of `fromId` method with hardcoded values might need a review to ensure it aligns with versioning practices.

The removal of `preUnsignedLong` and `postUnsignedLong` versions might affect test coverage. Ensure that the new approach using `PRE_UNSIGNED_LONG` and `POST_UNSIGNED_LONG` covers all necessary scenarios.

The changes in `TextFormatTests` replace hardcoded index names and versions with constants. Ensure that these changes do not introduce any unintended behavior and align with the project's naming conventions.

The removal of `INTRODUCING_UNSIGNED_LONG_TRANSPORT` without a corresponding update or reference elsewhere might lead to issues if this constant is used elsewhere in the codebase. Ensure that all references to this constant are updated accordingly.

The method `isClientCompatible` has been moved and refactored into `onOrAfter`. However, the logic seems to have changed slightly. The original method also checked if the major version difference was at most one unit behind the server's version. This check is missing in the new implementation. Ensure that this change does not introduce any unintended behavior.

The changes in `DriverManagerRegistrationTests` and `VersionParityTests` replace `Version.CURRENT` with `VersionTests.current()`. Ensure that `VersionTests.current()` returns the correct version and behaves as expected in all test scenarios.

The changes in `CliSessionTests` replace version generation logic with random versions from a filtered list. Ensure that this change maintains the intended test coverage and does not introduce any unintended behavior.

The changes in `SysTypesTests`, `ShowColumns`, and `SqlSession` replace `Version.fromId(cmd.v2().configuration().version().id)` or `Version.fromId(session.configuration().version().id)` with `cmd.v2().configuration().version()` or `session.configuration().version()`. Ensure that this change does not introduce any unintended behavior, especially if the version object is used in a way that relies on its ID.

The methods `supportsUnsignedLong`, `supportsVersionType`, and `supportsDateNanos` have been moved to `VersionCompatibility`. Ensure that these methods are used consistently across the codebase and that their logic is correct.

review_comment: main is now v9, which can only talk to 8.17 nodes (when released). Does this mean we can remove all these versions, or are these actually _client_ versions which still need to be compatible? Is this documented somewhere?

> Is this documented somewhere?

The  the current version compatibility policy has been documented [here](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/sql-jdbc.html#jdbc-compatibility). This has been applying to the 7.x and 8.x.

Given the SQL maintenance status, this PR proposes updating this policy by allowing unrestricted connectivity between clients and servers past 8.16 (comment [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/112094/files#diff-35b51352875c23b3a8029fab7ad54b93bb9363c8d5a14bfd61992a534a3e86edR28-R32)). Any pre-8.16 releases (including all 8.15 releases to follow) will have to comply with the exiting policy (linked above).
The SL releases will be considered at version 8.16 (the "server compatibility version").

> Does this mean we can remove all these versions.

The versions should remain in the 8.x branch, but those 7.x not referenced explicitly in `VersionCompatibility` class (I think it's just `SqlVersions.V_7_12_0`) could be removed on 9.x. I think this would be done after back porting to 8.x though.

> are these actually client versions which still need to be compatible?

Yes, the post 7.7.0 client releases would need to stay compatible with 8.x servers.

> those 7.x not referenced explicitly in VersionCompatibility class (I think it's just SqlVersions.V_7_12_0) could be removed on 9.x

This could be an `@UpdateForV9` tag on the 7.0.0 version/SqlVersion class.

I think it's worth a descriptive comment at this point, that no further versions should be added in the normal course of things.
